description: The line plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC) percentage of different models as a function of the co-occurrence number. The x-axis, labeled "Co-occurrence Number," is on a logarithmic scale ranging from 10^0 to 10^3. The y-axis, labeled "ACC (%)", ranges from 0 to 55. The plot includes six lines representing different models: Base (black line with circle markers), MEND (brown line with diamond markers), FT (blue line with triangle markers), IKE (red line with triangle markers), and ROME (green line with square markers). The Base model shows a relatively flat trend, maintaining an accuracy just above 30% across all co-occurrence numbers. The MEND model shows a slight increase in accuracy as the co-occurrence number increases, starting just above 30% and ending just below 40%. The FT model shows a more pronounced increase, starting at around 35% and ending at approximately 45%. The IKE model follows a similar trend to the FT model, starting at around 35% and ending at around 45%. The ROME model shows the most significant increase, starting at around 30% and ending at just above 55%.
